info.title: Snappr API
info.summary: Commission photoshoots, editing jobs and Magic Jobs, and retrieve the resulting images and videos.
info.description:
The Snappr API is available to Snappr for Enterprise customers. It lets you check coverage and
availability, create and track photoshoot bookings, editing jobs and Magic Jobs, and download
the delivered images and videos.

Human-readable documentation: https://docs.snappr.com

Every list endpoint returns the same envelope: `results`, `count` (items in this page),
`limit`, `offset` and `total` (items across all pages). Page through with `limit` and `offset`.

Errors are JSON objects with a machine-readable `code` (see the `Error` schema).

Each API key can make 1,000 requests per minute. Every response carries the IETF `RateLimit-Policy`
and `RateLimit` headers, and a `429` response adds `Retry-After`
(https://docs.snappr.com/#rate-limits).

The current version is `1.0.0`, sent in the optional `accept-version` header. Additive changes (new
endpoints, optional parameters, response fields, error codes and values) ship without a new version.
Deprecated parameters and fields are marked `deprecated: true` in this spec
(https://docs.snappr.com/#versioning-and-deprecation).

get.description:
Returns whether Snappr has photographer coverage for a location and shoot type. Coverage is
independent of specific dates or times; use `getAvailability` for bookable start times.

Provide either `latitude` and `longitude`, or `address`. If both are provided, only
`latitude` and `longitude` are used.

parameters.name: shoottype
parameters.description: Shoot type `name` (see `listShootTypes`), e.g. `event`. When omitted, coverage is checked across all shoot types.

parameters.name: creator_id
parameters.description: Check whether this specific creator covers the location.

400.description: The request was invalid, or could not be fulfilled (validation failure, no coverage, no availability, location outside your region).

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid, or its user is not an admin of the account.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (1,000 requests per minute per API key). Retry after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

500.description: Unexpected server error. Try again later.

get.description:
Returns available shoot start times for a location, local date, shoot type and duration.
All times within the local date are returned, formatted in UTC.

Provide either `latitude` and `longitude`, or `address`. If both are provided, only
`latitude` and `longitude` are used. Always check availability before creating a booking
with `start_at` set.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Length of the shoot in minutes.

parameters.name: days_span
parameters.description: Number of consecutive days, starting at `date`, to return availability for.

parameters.name: creator_id
parameters.description: Return availability for this specific creator only.

post.description:
Creates a photoshoot booking. There are two ways to create one:

1. Provide all details including `start_at`. The end-customer is notified once the booking is placed.
2. Set `start_at` to `null`. Snappr contacts the end-customer (email and/or mobile phone) to pick a
   date and time, and the response includes a `scheduling_url` they can use. `start_at` cannot be
   `null` when `creator_id` is set.

Provide either `latitude` and `longitude`, or `address`. If both are provided, only `latitude` and
`longitude` are used. Booking a time with no available photographer returns a `400` with code
`NotAvailable`; an account without enough credits gets `402` `InsufficientCredits`.

For a `food` booking you can optionally send the restaurant's `restaurant_name`,
`restaurant_address` and `source_url`, and `menu_items` (see `MenuItemCreate`) to get a per-item
report in the booking's `menu_items` (see `MenuItem`). The response echoes your items straight
away, each `pending` with its own `uid`. When the booking is `completed`, Snappr matches your
items to the delivered images by `internal_id`, falling back to name; sending items doesn't
guarantee images of them.

`restaurant_name`, `restaurant_address`, `source_url` and `menu_items` only apply when `shoottype`
is `food`. Sent with any other `shoottype`, they are ignored: not validated, not stored and not
echoed in the response, and the request succeeds. When `shoottype` is `food`, returns
`400 ValidationError` when `menu_items` has more than 1000 items, when two items share an
`internal_id`, or when an item is missing its `internal_id` or `name`.

value.title: Emerald Theatre Shoot
value.location_notes: Location is Emerald Theatre - ring buzzer at main entrance on arrival
value.style_notes: Shots of as many members of crowd as possible; shallow depth of field where possible

value.title: Sample Bistro Menu Shoot
value.location_notes: Sample Bistro - ask for the manager at the front counter on arrival
value.style_notes: One hero shot per dish on a plain table; natural light where possible

get.description:
Lists the delivered images of a booking. The booking must have status `completed`; otherwise the request fails with `400` code `BadRequest`.

On a booking that has `menu_items`, each image also lists the menu items it shows: one image can
belong to several items (e.g. one photo for several sizes of a pizza), and `menu_item_uids` joins
it to the booking's `menu_items`.

post.description:
Creates a Magic Job. It is returned with status `created`; Snappr then locates the business's
listing, generates the images and delivers them in one or more batches. Each delivery triggers an
`images_delivered` webhook event.

For a `menu` job you can optionally send `menu_items` (see `MenuItemCreate`) to get a per-item
report in the job's `menu_items` (see `MenuItem`). The response echoes your items straight away,
each `pending` with its own `uid`. Snappr still builds the image set from the restaurant's store
page and matches your items to the delivered images by `internal_id`, falling back to name;
sending items doesn't guarantee images for them.

`restaurant_name`, `restaurant_address` and `menu_items` only apply when `type` is `menu`. Sent with
any other `type`, they are ignored: not validated, not stored and not echoed in the response, and
the request succeeds. When `type` is `menu`, returns `400 ValidationError` when `menu_items` has
more than 1000 items, when two items share an `internal_id`, or when an item is missing its
`internal_id` or `name`.

get.description:
Retrieves one Magic Job. A job moves through `created`, `in_progress`, `completed` and `failed`.
It stays `in_progress` while further deliveries are expected and becomes `completed` once all
images are delivered, at which point `completed_at` and `images_count` are populated. Failed
jobs are followed up by your account manager. `menu_items` reports which menu items got images
(see `MenuItem`).

get.description:
Lists the current complete set of delivered images for a Magic Job, across all delivery batches.
Each result is one image, which can belong to several menu items (e.g. one photo for several
sizes of a pizza); `menu_item_uids` joins it to the job's `menu_items`. If Snappr replaces an
image after delivery it keeps its `uid` (the stable handle for diffing) while `internal_ids` and
URLs may change. URLs are signed and expire at `url_expires_at`; call again for freshly signed URLs.

1. Provide the source `images`.
2. Set `images` to `null` and provide `uploader_firstname` and `uploader_email`. Snappr contacts

post.description:
Sent to your custom webhook URL (set in the Snappr portal under API → Custom Webhook) every time a
booking is created or updated. All event families share one URL: dispatch on which resource key is
present (`booking`, `magic_job`) and ignore event types or payload shapes you don't recognise.

200.description: Return any 2xx status to acknowledge the event.

post.summary: Magic Job delivered a batch of images
post.description:
Sent every time a Magic Job delivers a batch of images. A job can deliver several batches, so
several events may arrive for the same `magic_job.uid`, each with a different `delivery_uid`.
Treat every delivery the same way: call `listMagicJobImages` and replace what you stored for that job.

200.description: Return any 2xx status to acknowledge the event.

bearerAuth.description:
Send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Get or regenerate the key in the Snappr
portal; each user has one active key and regenerating it deactivates the previous one. The sandbox
uses a separate sandbox key.

AcceptVersion.name: accept-version
AcceptVersion.description: API version. The only version is `1.0.0`, which is also the default. See https://docs.snappr.com/#versioning-and-deprecation.

Latitude.name: latitude
Latitude.description: Latitude of the shoot location. Required together with `longitude` when `address` is not provided.

Longitude.name: longitude
Longitude.description: Longitude of the shoot location. Required together with `latitude` when `address` is not provided.

Address.name: address
Address.description: Address of the shoot location, as a Google Maps–valid address. Required when `latitude` and `longitude` are not provided.
Address.example: Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center, San Francisco, CA, USA

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Number of items to skip, for pagination.

MediaLimit.name: limit
MediaLimit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

TypeLimit.name: limit
TypeLimit.description: Maximum number of types to return.

RateLimit-Policy.description: The rate-limit quota, as an IETF `RateLimit-Policy` field. `q` is the number of requests allowed per window of `w` seconds.

RateLimit.description: The quota left, as an IETF `RateLimit` field. `r` is the number of requests remaining in the current window, which resets in `t` seconds. Each API server keeps its own count, so `r` is an estimate and can go up between requests.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before sending another request.

Error.description:
Error response. `code` is one of: `ValidationError`, `BadRequest`, `NoCoverage`, `NotAvailable`,
`OutsideRegion`, `CreatorNotFound`, `Unauthorized`, `InsufficientCredits`, `NotFound`, `RateLimit`,
`UnknownError`, `ServerError`. New codes may be added.

count.description: Number of items in this page.

total.description: Number of items across all pages.

coverage.description: Whether Snappr has coverage for this location and shoot type.

available_providers.description: Number of photographers covering the location.

available_specialist_providers.description: Number of those who specialise in the shoot type.

available_related_specialist_providers.description: Number of those who specialise in the shoot type or a related one.

available_times.description: Available shoot start times, in UTC.

latitude.description: Latitude of the shoot location. Required together with `longitude` when `address` is not provided.

longitude.description: Longitude of the shoot location. Required together with `latitude` when `address` is not provided.

address.description: Google Maps–valid address of the shoot location. Required when `latitude` and `longitude` are not provided.

start_at.description: Shoot start time in UTC. Must be present; set to `null` to have the end-customer pick the date and time.

location_notes.description: Details to help the photographer find the location and contact person.

style_notes.description: Instructions, stylistic preferences and special requests.

internal_id.description: Your own identifier, for matching the booking with your data.

creator_id.description: Assign the booking to this specific creator.

tags.description: Tags for finding and reporting on bookings in the Snappr portal. Each tag is lowercased, trimmed and truncated to 255 characters.

restaurant_name.description: Name of the restaurant as it appears on your platform. If omitted, `title` is used. Only applies when `shoottype` is `food`; ignored for any other shoot type.

restaurant_address.description: Full address of the restaurant as a single string. If omitted, `address` is used. Only applies when `shoottype` is `food`; ignored for any other shoot type.

source_url.description: URL of the restaurant's store page on your platform. Only applies when `shoottype` is `food`; ignored for any other shoot type.

menu_items.description:
The items on the restaurant's menu, for a per-item report in the booking's `menu_items`. Only applies
when `shoottype` is `food`; ignored, and not validated, for any other shoot type. `[]` is the same as
omitting the field. Each item's `internal_id` must be unique within the list.

package_id.description: The Snappr package (product) the booking was placed on.

creator_name.description: Assigned photographer's first name and last initial.

restaurant_name.description: Present only on a `food` booking created with `restaurant_name`.

restaurant_address.description: Present only on a `food` booking created with `restaurant_address`.

source_url.description: Present only on a `food` booking created with `source_url`.

menu_items.description:
Per-item report: which menu items got images. Present only on a `food` booking created with a
non-empty `menu_items` list; omitted otherwise (unlike a Magic Job, a booking never lists discovered
items when you sent none). Every item is `pending` until the booking is `completed`. Then each item
you sent becomes `delivered` or `not_found`, and the items Snappr found in the images that you didn't
send are added (`provided: false`). Items you sent come first, in the order you sent them.

update_at.description: Misspelled alias of `updated_at`, kept for backwards compatibility.

scheduling_url.description: Present when `start_at` was `null`. Link the end-customer uses to pick a date and time.

bookingTags.description: The tags stored on the booking (normalised from the request's `tags`).

internal_ids.description:
The `internal_id`s of the menu items this image shows, skipping items whose `internal_id` is `null`.
Present only on a booking that has `menu_items`. Can be empty, e.g. for a photo of the restaurant
itself. Treat as opaque strings.

menu_item_uids.description:
The `uid`s of the menu items in the booking's `menu_items` that this image shows. Present only on a
booking that has `menu_items`. One image can belong to several items, e.g. several sizes of a pizza.

restaurant_name.description: Name of the restaurant as it appears on your platform. Required when `type` is `menu`; ignored for any other type.

restaurant_address.description: Full address of the restaurant as a single string. Required when `type` is `menu`; ignored for any other type.

internal_id.description: Your restaurant's or menu's ID, for matching the job with your data.

source_url.description: URL of the restaurant's store page on your platform. If omitted, Snappr locates it from the name, address and `internal_id`.

menu_items.description:
The items on the restaurant's menu, for a per-item report in the job's `menu_items`. Only applies
when `type` is `menu`; ignored, and not validated, for any other type. `[]` is the same as omitting
the field. Each item's `internal_id` must be unique within the list.

source_platform.description: Platform Snappr found the listing on.

internal_id.description: Your restaurant's or menu's ID, as you sent it.

images_count.description: Number of delivered images. Present only when `status` is `completed`.

menu_items.description:
Per-item report: which menu items got images. Present on every `menu` job. Items you sent come
first, in the order you sent them, followed by the items Snappr discovered on the source platform.
If you sent no `menu_items`, it holds only discovered items: `[]` on a new job, growing as images
are delivered.

MenuItemCreate.description:
One menu item you send in `menu_items` when you create a Magic Job whose `type` is `menu` or a
booking whose `shoottype` is `food`; with any other type or shoot type, `menu_items` is ignored.
No endpoint reads or writes menu items directly. A list takes at most 1000 items, each item's
`internal_id` must be unique within it, and `[]` is the same as omitting the field. On a `menu`
Magic Job or a `food` booking, returns `400 ValidationError` when the list has more than 1000
items, when two items share an `internal_id`, or when an item is missing its `internal_id` or
`name`. Snappr reports on each item in the Magic Job's or booking's `menu_items` (see `MenuItem`).

internal_id.description: Your ID for the item. Unique within `menu_items`. Treated as an opaque string.

MenuItem.description:
One menu item in the per-item report of a Magic Job or a booking. Menu items only exist on a Magic
Job whose `type` is `menu` and on a booking whose `shoottype` is `food`. No endpoint reads or writes
them directly: they are returned inside the Magic Job or booking.

Every item you send starts as `pending`. Snappr matches each one to the delivered images by
`internal_id`, falling back to name. An item with at least one image is `delivered`; on a booking,
matching happens when the booking is `completed`, so every item stays `pending` until then. Once
the Magic Job or booking is `completed`, an item you sent with no images becomes `not_found`.
Items Snappr found but you didn't send are added with `provided: false` and are always
`delivered`. On a Magic Job, these discovered items appear as images are delivered; on a booking,
when it is `completed`. The report doesn't guarantee images for the items you send.

Once the Magic Job or booking is `completed`, every item falls into one of three groups: `provided`
and `delivered` (you sent it and it got images), `provided` and `not_found` (you sent it and Snappr
found no image for it), or not `provided` (Snappr discovered it). Items you sent come first, in the
order you sent them. Join images to items with each image's `menu_item_uids`.

uid.description: Snappr's stable identifier for the item, generated and controlled by Snappr. It never changes.

internal_id.description:
Your ID for the item, as you sent it. For a discovered item, the ID Snappr found for it (on a Magic
Job, the item's ID on the source platform), or `null` if there is none.

name.description:
Name of the item, as you sent it. For a discovered item, the name Snappr found for it (on a Magic
Job, the same as the image's `menu_item_name`).

description.description: Description of the item, as you sent it; `null` if you sent none. Always `null` for a discovered item.

provided.description:
`true` if you sent the item in `menu_items`. `false` if Snappr discovered it (on a Magic Job, on
the source platform); a discovered item is always `delivered`.

status.description:
`pending`: no images yet and the Magic Job or booking is not `completed`. `delivered`: at least
one image. `not_found`: the Magic Job or booking is `completed` and the item has no images.

images_count.description:
Number of delivered images linked to the item. An image that belongs to several items counts towards
each of them, so the items' counts can add up to more than the total number of delivered images.

uid.description: Stable identifier; kept if the image is replaced.

internal_ids.description: The menu items' identifier(s) in your catalog, as found on the source platform, or from your submitted menu item when Snappr matched it by name. Treat as opaque strings.

menu_item_uids.description: The `uid`s of the menu items in the job's `menu_items` that this image belongs to. One image can belong to several items, e.g. several sizes of a pizza.

internal_id.description: Your own identifier, for matching the job with your data.

images.description: Source images. Set to `null` to have a third-party uploader provide them, in which case `uploader_firstname` and `uploader_email` are required.

min_photo_number.description: Minimum number of photos the third-party uploader must upload.

max_photo_number.description: Maximum number of photos the third-party uploader may upload. Must be greater than `min_photo_number`.
